summary.done: Added Voice struct (Enabled bool, Voices map[string]string) to Settings in internal/config/settings.go with json tag 'voice'; added NormalizeVoice() which seeds voices.en/voices.fr to 'jane' when missing and initializes a nil Voices map; LoadSettings now calls NormalizeVoice on both the file-missing and parsed paths. Added internal/config/settings_test.go covering all three acceptance criteria plus no-file and empty-map cases.
summary.tradeoffs: NormalizeVoice is a method on *Settings called from LoadSettings rather than a package-level helper — keeps it discoverable next to the struct but means any future non-LoadSettings construction path must remember to call it.
summary.decisions: Used map[string]string for voices (per design snippet) so extra languages can be added without struct changes; normalization only fills en/fr defaults and never overwrites user-set values; invalid names pass through untouched per acceptance criterion.
summary.lessons_learned: LoadSettings previously returned zero-value Settings silently when settings.json was absent — that path also needed normalization, not just the parse path.

summary.failures: None in this verify round: all four verification commands passed on first run (go test, go test -race, go build ./..., go vet). Prior session fixed three real bugs found during implementation: (1) Speaker.Speak deferred context cancellation at return, which killed the async child immediately after Speak returned — ownership of cancel now transfers to the process watcher goroutine; (2) double-lock deadlock risk in Emit when the out-of-lock onPreempt hook re-enters the coordinator — admission is serialized by a dedicated emitMu so hooks can safely call CancelGroup while mu is released; (3) queued same-group chunks were not released FIFO after the playing chunk finished — finishChunkLocked now pops exactly one waiter and invokes it.
summary.done: internal/voice package with two layers. voice.go: Speaker (DetectLanguage via bounded-timeout POST /detect, resolveVoice fallback chain lang→prevLang→en, Speak spawning squid-tts-say -v <name> -q --stdin with Setpgid and stdin pipe, Process wrapper with Done/Err/Pid/Kill killing the whole group via kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)). coordinator.go: Coordinator owning group state (StartGroup/Emit/EndGroup/CancelGroup/Current) with muted-drop, back-to-back within group via waiter queue, cross-group bump through swappable onPreempt policy hook defaulting to CancelGroup. EndGroup closes admission only (accepted chunks drain); CancelGroup mutes, kills the playing group's process tree, drops waiters, and drops all future chunks for that ID. 17 tests in voice_test.go covering every acceptance criterion deterministically: fake TTS detect server (httptest), recording shell CLIs instead of live TTS/aplay, explicit stale-callback injection for the watcher guard, and a real Linux /proc-based process-group kill test verifying no orphaned child.
summary.tradeoffs: Emit returns nil (not an error) for dropped chunks (muted/ended/unknown groups) per design — callers cannot distinguish drop from success, acceptable since drops are silent by spec. Detect failures are swallowed into the fallback chain rather than surfaced, so a wedged server degrades silently to the previous-language voice. SpeakTimeout (60s) bounds the whole pipeline but long sentences rely on cancellation for earlier teardown. endGroup-on-hanging-player requires an explicit CancelGroup to stop playback (documented in tests).
summary.decisions: One short-lived process per chunk (no persistent stream) keeps lifecycle simple and makes group kill trivial. Two locks (emitMu + mu): emitMu serializes admission across the out-of-lock policy hook, mu protects state; this avoids both deadlock and lost updates when the hook re-enters. Stale-watcher guard compares g.player == p under lock so a delayed completion callback can never clear a newer group's current state. CLI resolved from PATH at NewSpeaker time (never hardcoded), overridable via SpeakerOptions.CLIPath for tests. Mute is per-group, not sticky across groups.
summary.lessons_learned: Async process ownership: when a function spawns a background process and returns, any context whose lifetime ends at return must NOT own the cancellation — defer cancel() in the spawner kills the child the instant the caller moves on. Ownership must transfer explicitly to the goroutine that waits on the process. Second lesson: any policy hook invoked outside a lock that may re-enter the same object needs either its own admission mutex or fully lock-free re-entrancy; releasing the state lock around the hook without an outer serialization point is a deadlock/waiter-release trap.

summary.failures: None — all tests pass including race detector.
summary.done: SentenceChunker implementing Chunker interface (Feed/Flush/ArmHoldTimer/Cancel) with sentence-boundary strategy: split on . ! ? \n, hold fragments under minWords and merge with next, max-hold timer via owned time.Timer with watcher goroutine, max-words force-flush with overflow held for next merge. Strategy params (minWords, maxHold, maxWords, boundaries) are constructor args. Timer lifecycle: rearmLocked stops+resets on each Feed; stopTimerOnlyLocked preserves cb when no fragment held; disarmLocked (Flush/Cancel) clears cb and stops watcher. Generation counter guards stale firings. Test seam: FireHeld + injectable timerIface with manual channel-based holdTimer for deterministic expiry without wall-clock polling.
summary.tradeoffs: Watcher captures timer.C() once at start; if timer is replaced (test injection after start), the old channel is used — acceptable because production never replaces the timer post-construction and tests inject before ArmHoldTimer. Merge emits when combined >= minWords (not strictly >), matching the passing bullet-merge tests.
summary.decisions: Owned timer per chunker instance (not shared); watcher goroutine lifetime tied to chunker via watcherDone channel closed by stopWatcherLocked. Empty (0-word) boundary fragments pass through mergeLocked harmlessly. Flush sets flushed flag so next Feed starts fresh cycle.
summary.lessons_learned: Timer callback ownership: ArmHoldTimer must preserve cb across 'no fragment held yet' states (stopTimerOnly vs disarm). Watcher must snapshot C() under lock to avoid nil-deref when Cancel nils the timer. Manual test timers need a real channel (not nil C()) so the async watcher path is exercised identically to production.

1.4.name: Wire narration into the assistant stream

summary.failures: None — go test ./internal/app, go build ./..., go vet, and go test -race (narration subset) all pass on final run.
summary.done: New internal/app/narration.go: Narrator (one speech group per assistant message) with beginMessage/feedDelta/endMessage/cancelActive over the voice.Coordinator + SentenceChunker. Wired into Model (app.go): narrator built in app.New via newVoiceCoordinator (degrades to inert no-op if squid-tts-say is not on PATH), voiceOn mirrors settings.Voice.Enabled for the future alt+v toggle. Stream hooks (stream.go): setStreamMode begins a group; LoopContinue feeds event.Text deltas into the chunker so the first sentence speaks while later ones are still generating; terminal LoopDone ends the group (final flush + EndGroup) before setChatMode; error/cancel paths (LoopError, cancelled LoopDone, ToolEventCancelled, ToolEventError) cancel the active group without flushing its buffer. Session switch (loadUISession) and shutdown (quitCmd) call cancelActive. Group state lives on the Model's Narrator, NOT in UIStreamState, so UIStreamState.reset() between tool phases cannot touch it — verified by test that chunks fed across a reset land in the same group. Six tests in narration_test.go using a recording fake TTS CLI (no aplay/server needed).
summary.tradeoffs: Emit errors (TTS server down, spawn failure) are swallowed silently — voice is best-effort and must never surface as a TUI error or interrupt the model stream; the downside is a wedged server degrades silently until the user notices no audio. Coordinator is built unconditionally at startup even when voice is disabled (cheap: one exec.LookPath); an inert narrator (nil coord) keeps all call sites guard-free. quitCmd's cancelActive runs synchronously before tea.Quit — clean kill, but a stuck player process would briefly delay exit (bounded by SIGKILL semantics, effectively instant).
summary.decisions: Group lifecycle tied to the MESSAGE, not the turn/tool context: begin in setStreamMode (covers both sendMessage and queued next-step restarts), end only at terminal LoopDone; ToolEventDone deliberately does NOT end the group because the continuation belongs to the same logical assistant message (design: group survives UIStreamState.reset()). Cancelled/error turns use cancelActive (kill + drop buffer) rather than endMessage (flush) so aborted utterances stop immediately instead of speaking the half-finished tail. Voice uses context.Background() for Emit, independent of the turn context, satisfying 'mute never cancels the stream'. prevLang tracking left for task 3.1 (Speak gets "" today → en fallback).
summary.lessons_learned: The coordinator's EndGroup closes admission, not playback: after EndGroup, Current() stays nonzero until the last accepted chunk's process exits and finishChunkLocked clears it — drain-wait assertions must poll Current()==0, not assert it immediately after EndGroup. A second lesson from the same trap: a group whose held fragment never became a chunk has Current()==0 even though the group exists, so tests asserting 'active group' must feed a >=min-words sentence first.

summary.failures: None — go test -count=1 ./internal/app and go build ./... pass; go vet clean.
summary.done: alt+v key binding (keymap.go) mirroring thinking; /voice on|off slash command registered in AllCommands with Keys wired so matchCommandKey fires it from both chat and streaming modes via the existing executeCommandByName path (no input.go changes needed). SlashCommand gained an Args field and OnExecute now takes (Model, []string); executeCommandByName validates args against the declared set and prints a usage notification for unknown values — this is the argument-handling extension the task asked for. New internal/app/voice_toggle.go: toggleVoice(args) flips the runtime voiceOn flag (bare = flip, on/off = explicit), never writes the settings file (settings stay the startup source of truth), prints 'voice on'/'voice off' feedback via setNotification, and on toggling OFF calls narrator.cancelActive() so mid-speech playback dies immediately (CancelGroup kills the player process group and mutes late chunks). Help overlay (internal/ui/help.go) lists alt+v in Chat & Streaming and /voice with its shortcut in Commands. Two tests in voice_toggle_test.go: flip semantics across bare/on/off, and off-mid-speech killing an in-flight chunk (real coordinator + fake TTS CLI + httptest detect server) with late-chunk drop verification.
summary.tradeoffs: executeCommandByName's signature change ripples to all 11 existing OnExecute closures (now take _ []string) — mechanical but touches every command; alternative was a separate arg-carrying dispatch path, which would have duplicated the BlockDuringStream/notification logic. /voice is NOT BlockDuringStream: toggling must work mid-stream (that is exactly when you want to shut it up or switch it on).
summary.decisions: Runtime-only toggle: voiceOn lives on Model, settings.Voice.Enabled untouched by the toggle (per acceptance criterion). Toggle-off uses narrator.cancelActive() (kill + mute, no flush) rather than endMessage so a half-finished sentence stops instantly instead of speaking its tail. Explicit args override current state (idempotent on/off) while bare invocation flips — matches the thinking UX plus the spec's '/voice on|off'.
summary.lessons_learned: Coordinator.Current() only reflects groups with an admitted chunk in flight: StartGroup alone leaves it at 0, so 'active group' assertions must feed a real chunk first. And the SentenceChunker holds fragments under minWords (default 3): a single 3-word sentence like 'speaking now.' stays held until a second fragment merges — narration tests need two sentences to force emission.

summary.failures: None — go build ./..., go vet, and go test -count=1 (internal/app, internal/ui, internal/voice, internal/cli) all pass; race detector clean on the speaking-hook + stale-watcher tests.
summary.done: Coordinator speaking hook (internal/voice/coordinator.go): SetSpeakingHook(fn(on bool)) fires exactly on state transitions — on=true when the first chunk of any group starts playing (startChunkLocked), on=false from clearCurrentLocked (player exit, drain after EndGroup, kill via CancelGroup). Back-to-back chunks of the same group do NOT re-fire (no flicker); the hook runs outside mu so it can safely re-enter. UI: RenderStatusLine gained a speaking bool param and prepends '🔊 speaking…' to the left side (truncates with the notification, right chip reserved); row is now padded to exactly width columns. Model.voiceSpeaking field set only inside Update via new voiceSpeakingMsg posted by the coordinator hook through program.Send (never written from a background goroutine). Wiring: app.New builds the coordinator with a nil program; cli/tui.go calls model.WireVoiceSpeaking(program) after tea.NewProgram replaces the coordinator in place (narrator keeps its group state). Tests: 4 coordinator-level tests in voice_test.go (first-chunk start/exit edges, back-to-back no-flicker, kill-path clears, stale callback cannot clear newer group's indicator — using the playerFinished injection seam), 3 app-level tests in narration_test.go (indicator appears on first chunk while generating + clears on completion incl. the Update path; kill path never stuck on; bump scenario where a superseded group's late watcher cannot turn off the newer group's indicator), and TestRenderStatusLineSpeakingIndicator covering glyph presence/absence, coexistence with notification+chip, and narrow-width truncation.
summary.tradeoffs: The speaker emoji renders double-width in most fonts, so lipgloss.Width of the glyph string exceeds its rune count by one; the status row pads to width but a pure-rune length assertion is off-by-one when the glyph is present (tests assert ~width). Alternative was an ASCII-only marker ('♪ speaking…') which would be font-stable but less recognizable. WireVoiceSpeaking replaces the whole coordinator at program-creation time rather than adding a second hook-install point — safe because it happens before Run() and no groups exist yet, but it means a future code path that emits speech between app.New and program creation would speak without indicator updates.
summary.decisions: Indicator state lives on the Coordinator (single owner of playback truth), not on the Narrator or Model — the hook reports 'any audio plays' across ALL groups (narration AND future alerts from milestone 3), matching the acceptance wording. Transition-based firing (not per-chunk) keeps the indicator steady during multi-chunk messages. The hook posts a tea.Msg instead of writing Model directly: Bubble Tea requires single-goroutine Model mutation, and p.Send is the sanctioned cross-goroutine channel (same pattern as localinput socket delivery). Generation-ID guard requirement is satisfied structurally: the existing per-group player-identity check (g.player == p) plus the current-group check in finishChunkLocked means a stale watcher for a superseded group neither clears Current nor fires an off-transition — verified deterministically by injecting c.playerFinished(g1, old) after g2 took over.
summary.lessons_learned: lipgloss.Width vs len([]rune) diverge on emoji (double-width runes): full-row-width assertions must use lipgloss.Width or allow ±1 rune tolerance when styled emoji are involved. And when a feature needs a background goroutine to update TUI state, the correct seam is always program.Send(msg) + a case in Update — direct field writes from coordinator goroutines are a data race even if they appear harmless.

summary.done: Added 'squid-os voice stop' CLI command following the input.go pattern: new internal/cli/voice.go (voiceCmd + voiceSubCmd tree with stop/on/off, reusing discoverInstance/roundTrip/printReply and --instance/--session flags), registered in cli.go via registerVoiceCommands; added voice_stop op to localinput server dispatch (new VoiceStopFunc config hook, reply status cancelled|nothing_playing); app-side handler localVoiceStopMsg in update.go runs the identical narrator.cancelActive() CancelGroup path as alt+x, wired through StartLocalInputServer's push channel like the other socket callbacks. Narrator.cancelActive now returns bool so the reply can distinguish actual cancellation from a no-op.
summary.lessons_learned: The CLI test helper fakeStore needed a voiceActive flag + VoiceStop wiring to make the end-to-end CLI test deterministic; server test rewires srv.cfg.VoiceStop directly since startTestServer doesn't take it.
summary.decisions: Reused the existing socket protocol shape (Request{Op: voice_stop}) instead of inventing a new frame type; session resolution mirrors control ops (req.SessionID falling back to live session). cancelActive gained a bool return so the wire reply is honest about whether a group actually existed — all existing call sites ignore the value, zero behavior change for alt+x/stream paths.
summary.tradeoffs: on/off subcommands are stubs returning 'not implemented yet: use /voice inside the TUI' — scaffold only per task scope. VoiceStop callback returns false on the 5s UI timeout (treated as nothing_playing) rather than an error, keeping exit 0 for the best-effort voice contract.

summary.decisions: Detection result is posted via program.Send as langDetectedMsg and applied ONLY inside Update (Bubble Tea single-goroutine rule); the background goroutine never writes Model fields. Stale-result protection lives in LangStore.SetIfNewest (subID >= lastID check), so even out-of-order HTTP resolutions cannot clobber newer state. The posted value is store.Get() at completion time, which is always the newest accepted language. Fire-and-forget goroutine (no tea.Cmd) so queued-input admission (which returns bool, not cmds) can also trigger detection at admission time rather than boundary delivery.
summary.tradeoffs: langSeq is a per-Model counter (not persisted); session reload starts IDs fresh — harmless since LangStore is also fresh per process. Detection fires only when the voice coordinator exists (TTS CLI available); without it alerts default to en fallback downstream.
summary.done: Added internal/voice/detect.go (LangStore with Submit/SetIfNewest/Get + DetectLang helper with 500ms bounded deadline reusing Speaker.DetectLanguage). Wired Model.lastUserLang (written only in Update via langDetectedMsg posted through program.Send, same pattern as voiceSpeakingMsg) and fireUserLangDetect called from all three submission paths: sendMessage (stream.go), admitQueuedInput at admission (queued_input.go), sendLocalSocketMessage (local_input.go). Added Coordinator.Speaker() accessor. Tests: voice package covers FR detection, rapid-fire stale-drop ordering (FR resolves second but EN wins), failure/timeout leaving previous value intact, empty-result ignored; app package covers the full wiring incl. Update application.
summary.lessons_learned: newQueueTestModel does not initialize narrator/langStore — tests must set them explicitly. Model is passed by value through Update, so pointer fields (narrator, langStore) survive copies but scalar fields (lastUserLang) do not — seed scalars directly in tests instead of round-tripping through Update before wiring. Connection-refused to 127.0.0.1:1 fails fast (~ms), well under the 500ms deadline.

summary.decisions: Reused the existing fallbackLang constant from voice.go as the EN key instead of introducing a new 'en' literal; kept FormatAlert (pure template render) separate from AlertText (group-level text assembly) so later tasks can emit chunks without re-deriving language logic.
summary.tradeoffs: None — table is the single source; no call-site magic strings.
summary.done: Created internal/voice/alerts.go with the Event type (6 events), the single bilingual alerts table (~12 strings, EN+FR per event), FormatAlert(ev, lang, detail) which falls back to EN for unknown languages and interpolates {name}, and AlertText(ev, lastUserLang, detail) which appends raw English detail after the lead-in for Error events only. Added alerts_test.go with deterministic exact-string tests covering all 12 template strings, EN fallback for unknown/empty languages, {name} interpolation in both languages, error-detail appending, and non-error detail suppression.
summary.lessons_learned: strings.ReplaceAll with an empty replacement strips the placeholder entirely ('I loaded the skill .') — the test must expect that, not the raw template, when detail is empty.

3.3.name: Hook events into the voice coordinator
